selectionEntries.name: Roaming Performers

rules.name: Roaming Performers
rules.description:
You may add one of the following Harlequins units to your Army List:
● TROUPE MASTER
● SHADOWSEER
and one of either:
● LIGHT TROUPE
● DARK TROUPE
● TWILIGHT TROUPE
If you do add one or more of those units to your Army List, your Army Rules gains Mocking Misstep, Allegro Advance, Prismatic Pirouette and Kaleidoscopic Cavalcade.

selectionEntries.comment: ROAMING PERFORMERS CONTROL: this Configuration entry controls Harlequin availability only. Constructive validation for already-included Harlequin units lives on the local Harlequin entryLinks so errors render on the affected units.

selectionEntries.name: Additional Copy Costs

modifiers.value: Additional Copy Costs is automatically managed by the listbuilder and should appear only once. Remove any extra Additional Copy Costs entries.

selectionEntries.comment: ADDITIONAL COPY COSTS REV19 / GS17. Permanent required accounting entry. The single parent now exposes Troops and Other accounting children. Guardian Defenders, Rangers, and Windriders use independent 4 / 6 / 8 Troop normal-copy allowances; Other preserves the existing 1 / 2 / 3 arithmetic exactly. Roaming Performer Harlequin Troupes remain governed by their existing one-Troupe cap and shared Harlequin library semantics; they are not part of native Aeldari Troop duplicate arithmetic. No generated, free, attached-zero-point, or otherwise exempt native Troop unit exists in this catalogue. The parent retains automatic insertion, Required Additional Copy Costs Configuration, and duplicate-entry validation.

selectionEntries.name: Troops
selectionEntries.comment: TROOP COPY-COST LEDGER. Guardian Defenders, Rangers, and Windriders are three independent native Aeldari Troop copy families using the GS17 4 / 6 / 8 normal-copy allowance. Roaming Performer Harlequin Troupes are not included in this local arithmetic because Roaming Performers already limits the roster to one Light, Dark, or Twilight Troupe; they therefore cannot cross the Troop duplicate threshold here.

selectionEntries.name: Other
selectionEntries.comment: OTHER COPY-COST LEDGER. Contains all 96 pre-existing Other point modifiers unchanged, preserving the established 1 / 2 / 3 allowance across the same 16 native Other copy families.

catalogue.comment:
ADDITIONAL COPY COSTS
All native non-Rare Other units use the soft 1/2/3 copy allowance. Each excess copy contributes +20 Points to the permanent Additional Copy Costs Configuration entry. Affected units link to the canonical Game System unit-reminder rule.

CONSTRUCTIVE ERROR UX REV14
Migrated to Game System revision 11. Added constructive validation for Additional Copy Costs configuration, required Leader attachments, host Leader capacity, Rare limits, and Roaming Performers interactions while preserving existing points, loadouts, copy-cost arithmetic, categories, and shared Harlequin library structure.

REV16 NEW RECRUIT EXPORT COMPATIBILITY
Updated to Warhammer 40k Reforged Game System revision 12. All Points cost references now use New Recruit's canonical Warhammer 40,000 cost-type identifier 51b2-306e-1021-d207. No unit costs, loadouts, validation, Roaming Performers logic, Harlequin library links, categories, or Additional Copy Costs arithmetic were otherwise changed.

REV17 POLISH PASS
Added explicit model headers to anonymous single-model Aeldari units; renamed the Guardian Defenders model-set header to Guardian Defenders 1-10; removed Wraithlord Heavy Weapon 1/2 and Wraithknight arm/shoulder slot labels while preserving the separate mechanical choice lists; standardized atomic package display with '&', using meaningful-choice-first ordering for the two Howling Banshee Exarch packages; renamed Black Guardians’ Webway and Pathfinders sections from Paid Wargear to Unit Upgrade; and standardized three Rare-limit errors plus thirteen Leader host-limit errors. Roaming Performers, Harlequin library linkage, Additional Copy Costs, attachment mechanics, fixed minimum-size shells, points, categories, and all selection-entry names except the sixteen approved atomic package display names are otherwise unchanged.

REV18 RETROSPECTIVE POLISH PASS
Completed the four remaining source-authorized 2-or-3-model units that REV17 still retained as fixed minimum-size shells. Shining Spears now offer Shining Spear 3 for +60 Points with Twin Shuriken Catapult and Laser Lance; Shadow Spectres now offer Shadow Spectre 3 for +40 Points with Prism Rifle; Wraithguards now offer Wraithguard 3 for +50 Points with its own Wraithcannon / D-Scythe choice; and Wraithblades now offer Wraithblade 3 for +50 Points with its own Ghostswords / Ghostaxe & Forceshield choice. Replaced the obsolete live Phase 0.1 min-size TODO comments on those units with current variable-size notes and modernized the live Additional Copy Costs comment to version-agnostic shared Game System wording. REV17 historical provenance remains unchanged. Roaming Performers, Harlequin library linkage, existing IDs and SelectionEntry names, base loadouts, Leader attachment behavior, Rare validation, Additional Copy Costs arithmetic, points outside the four authorized added models, categories, and all other rules semantics remain unchanged.

REV19 / GS17 TROOP COPY COSTS
Updated to Game System revision 17 and adopted the unified Additional Copy Costs presentation with Troops and Other child ledgers. Guardian Defenders, Rangers, and Windriders now use separate Troop 4 / 6 / 8 normal-copy allowances; each further identical copy costs +20 Points. All 96 pre-existing Other point modifiers were moved unchanged to the Other child, preserving the same 16 native Other copy families. No zero-point, generated, attached-free, or otherwise exempt native Troop unit exists in this catalogue. Roaming Performers remains unchanged: it still permits only one Light, Dark, or Twilight Harlequin Troupe, so those imported shared units cannot generate a duplicate-Troop surcharge in an Aeldari roster and are not added to the local Troop ledger. The existing Harlequins Library catalogue link and all Roaming Performer entryLinks remain unchanged. All unrelated loadouts, Leader attachment behavior, variable-size units, Rare validation, Roaming Performers validation, and other catalogue mechanics remain unchanged.

REV20 — DARK REAPER EXARCH REAPER LAUNCHER
Added Reaper Launcher Starshot & Starswarm to the Dark Reaper Exarch's exclusive weapon selection and made it the default. The wording matches the existing Reaper Launcher Starshot & Starswarm option already used elsewhere in the catalogue. Tempest Launcher, Shuriken Cannon, and Aeldari Missile Launcher remain unchanged aside from sortIndex shifting to follow the new default option. No other unit or catalogue mechanic was changed.

REV21 — SHARED REAPER LAUNCHER EXPORT PACKAGE
Created one shared Reaper Launcher (Starshot & Starswarm) upgrade and converted every current catalogue use of that combined weapon to entryLinks targeting the same semantic ID: Autarch, Dark Reaper Exarch, and Dark Reapers 2-5. The four ordinary Dark Reapers now select quantity 4 of the shared package instead of locally named '4x Reaper Launcher Starshot' and '4x Starswarm' entries. The Exarch's shared launcher remains the default. The old Starswarm branch remains only as a hidden, unselected legacy shell so every pre-existing ID survives. No unrelated catalogue mechanic or unit was changed.

REV22 — SHARED BANSHEE BLADE & SHURIKEN PISTOL EXPORT PACKAGE
Created one shared Banshee Blade & Shuriken Pistol upgrade for Howling Banshees 2-5. The four ordinary Banshees now select actual quantity 4 of that shared package, replacing the previous separate '4x Banshee Blade' and '4x Shuriken Pistol' live selections. This allows New Recruit to export the fixed equipment as one consolidated '4x Banshee Blade & Shuriken Pistol' line. The old Banshee Blade ID remains the live entryLink ID and the old Shuriken Pistol branch is retained as a hidden legacy shell, so every pre-existing catalogue ID survives. No Exarch loadout, points, legality, copy-cost arithmetic, Reaper Launcher normalization, or unrelated unit was changed.

REV23 — EXPORT & LOADOUT CLEANUP
Renamed all live Aeldari Missile Launcher selections to Aeldari Missile Launcher (Starshot & Sunburst). Corrected Wraithlord to one melee choice between Wraithspear, Ghostglaive, and Wraithlord Fists while leaving its secondary and heavy weapon lists unchanged. Compressed Shining Spears into atomic model loadouts. Removed the exposed quantity controls from Dark Reapers 2-5 and Howling Banshees 2-5 while preserving their shared-ID quantity aggregation through hidden payload selections. Swooping Hawks 2-5 now use the atomic Lasblaster & Hawk’s Frag Grenade package and export at quantity 4. Existing IDs are preserved wherever the underlying concept remains live; superseded objects are retained as inert legacy shells.

REV24 — EXPORT PRESENTATION CLEANUP
Completed the Aeldari Missile Launcher naming pass by updating prefixed Twin/Hull variants to include (Starshot & Sunburst). Striking Scorpions 2-5 now use the atomic Shuriken Pistol & Scorpion Chainsword package at quantity 4. Fire Dragons now present Melta Bomb Wargear as five independent bearer checkboxes instead of five optional (None) selectors. Rangers 1-5 now use the atomic Ranger Long Rifle & Shuriken Pistol package at quantity 5. Existing IDs, costs, and unrelated mechanics are preserved.

REV25 — SHINING SPEAR EXARCH WORDING
Reordered the two Shining Spear Exarch atomic loadout names so the player-facing differentiator appears first: Star Lance & Shuriken Cannon and Paragon Sabre & Shuriken Cannon. No IDs, costs, defaults, or mechanics changed.

REV26 — TROOP RULE + FIXED ASPECT PACKAGE CLEANUP
Updated to Game System revision 20 and retargeted Guardian Defenders, Rangers, and Windriders to the Additional Copy Cost - Troop short-form rule. Replaced the older visible-one-plus-hidden-export-payload implementation for Striking Scorpions 2-5, Dark Reapers 2-5, Swooping Hawks 2-5, Howling Banshees 2-5, and Rangers 1-5 with literal fixed-count atomic packages: 4x / 5x as appropriate. The surviving visible selection IDs were preserved; obsolete hidden quantity payloads and dead legacy shells for those fixed blocks were removed. Autarch loadout formatting was audited and found normal, so it was left mechanically unchanged.
